Jorge Assis, PhD // Nord University, Norway // biodiversityDS, Centre of Marine Sciences, Portugal

Niche overlap

Probabilistic method

biodiversityDS .

Probabilistic method for quantifying n-dimensional niches.

# sources the needed functions and libraries
library(terra)
library(bDSSDMTools)
library(ecospat)

# load environmental predictors
rasterFiles <- list.files(path = "../Data/Raster data", pattern = "Present Surface", full.names = TRUE)
rasterFiles
## [1] "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface Nitrate Mean.tif"          
## [2] "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif"
## [3] "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMin.tif"
# produce raster stack of environmental predictors
environment <- rast(rasterFiles)
names(environment) <- c("Nitrate", "Temperature Max.", "Temperature Min")
S9 // Niche overlap analyses

biodiversityDS .
# load binary SDM outputs
speciesA <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Laminaria hyperborea Suitability.tif")
speciesB <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Laminaria ochroleuca Suitability.tif")

names(speciesA) <- "L. hyperborea"
names(speciesB) <- "L. ochroleuca"

# plot the suitability of Laminaria hyperborea
plot(speciesA, col = c("#97C3DF", "#0c2f4d"))

S9 // Niche overlap analyses

biodiversityDS .
# plot the suitability of Laminaria ochroleuca
plot(speciesB, col = c("#97C3DF", "#0c2f4d"))

S9 // Niche overlap analyses

biodiversityDS .
# computes the probabilistic approach for quantifying n-dimensional niche overlap. Shows
# the average environmental niche uses.
data <- prepareDataNicheOverlap(environment, speciesA, speciesB)
##         species  Nitrate Temperature Max. Temperature Min
## 1 L. hyperborea 2.566081         15.36822        5.187073
## 2 L. ochroleuca 1.322024         20.51024       11.794850
S9 // Niche overlap analyses
biodiversityDS .

# plot niche overlap and determine niche size
nicheSize(data, nsamples = 100, colors = c("#97C3DF", "#0c2f4d"))

##     L. hyperborea L. ochroleuca
## est    1564.25668    1406.51311
## se       21.50407      25.58158
S9 // Niche overlap analyses
biodiversityDS .

# plot niche overlap as the probability of species displayed in rows overlapping onto those
# displayed in columns.
meanNicheOverlap(data, nsamples = 100, colors = c("#97C3DF", "#0c2f4d"))
##                Species B
## Species A       L. hyperborea L. ochroleuca
##   L. hyperborea            NA         64.89
##   L. ochroleuca          53.7            NA

S9 // Niche overlap analyses
biodiversityDS .

D and I alternative methods

# Prepare data for niche overlap analyses
grid.clim <- prepareDataNicheOverlap2(environment, speciesA, speciesB)

S9 // Niche overlap analyses
biodiversityDS .

# niche overlap analyses. Both D and I provide a value between 0 (no overlap) and 1
# (complete overlap), making it easy to interpret and compare.
ecospat.niche.overlap(grid.clim$grid.clim.sp.1, grid.clim$grid.clim.sp.2, cor = F)
## $D
## [1] 0.4200789
## 
## $I
## [1] 0.6177362
S9 // Niche overlap analyses

biodiversityDS .
# Equivalency test: Failed to reject the null hypothesis (p > 0.05) - the groups occupy
# statistically indistinguishable ecological niches.
eq.test <- ecospat.niche.equivalency.test(grid.clim$grid.clim.sp.1, grid.clim$grid.clim.sp.2,
    rep = 1000)
eq.test$p.D
## [1] 0.000999001
eq.test$p.I
## [1] 0.4855145
S9 // Niche overlap analyses
